summary: Three place-and-route iterations were run for uart. Iteration 1 (density 55%) had 3 max-fanout violations. Iteration 2 (density 60%) had 1. Iteration 3 (CTS_DISTANCE_BETWEEN_BUFFERS 0 to 25) shows 0 max-fanout, slew and cap violations, 0 route DRC errors, 0 antenna violating nets/pins and 0 disconnected pins in the iteration data, with positive setup and hold slack on all 9 corners. Two things stay open for a human: the CTS report shows a hold slack of -0.002920 ns at nom_ff_n40C_1v95 right after CTS (before the final iteration-3 numbers), and no congestion/overflow figure is present in the inputs. The runtime still has to run the real checks.
assumptions: Escaped defects are reported as none in the inputs; no explicit escaped-defect field exists.
Hold/setup slack was only supplied for the three nom_* corners, so nothing is claimed for min_* and max_* corners.
Iteration 3 in pnr_report.json is the final post-route state.
Latency quoted is source_latency_ns from the setup view; no separate per-clock-pin latency was supplied.
No budget figure is in the inputs, so spend versus budget and a weekly forecast are not stated.
Only one clock (clk) exists per the spec, so tool metrics are attributed to clk.
Placement density is quoted in percent as PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT; utilization values are the fractions given by the tools (floorplan 0.469189, iteration 3 final 0.503243).

The 'changes' field of iterations 1 and 2 is not consistent with each record's 'params'. Iteration 1 params show PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT 55.0 but its change lists 60, and iteration 2 params already show 60 with a change that again lists 60. I read iteration 1's change as the one that produced iteration 2's setup, and iteration 2's entry as a restatement of that change. Iteration 3's change (CTS_DISTANCE_BETWEEN_BUFFERS 25) matches iteration 3's params.

The CTS report (cts_report.json, marked iteration 3) is read as post-CTS data. Its hold slack after CTS (-0.002920 ns at nom_ff) comes from an earlier flow point than the iteration 3 post-route hold slack (+0.11045037419512992 ns at nom_ff); I do not reconcile the two.
The final state is iteration 3, the last record in pnr_iterations.json, and its 'facts' are post-route values (DRC and antenna are route-stage fields).
The iteration table follows each iteration's params, because the changes fields of iterations 1 and 2 disagree with them.
The reported 'worst' figures below are the minimum over the 9 corners listed in the tool data; I computed no new values.
Tree skew (reported skew minus 0.25 ns uncertainty) is taken as the physical skew; the tool gives both values.
